statements.subject: server
statements.description: Every command MUST generate exactly one reply.
actions: Generate exactly one reply per command received

statements.subject: client
statements.description: Since, in violation of this specification, the text is sometimes not sent, clients that do not receive it SHOULD be prepared to process the code alone (with or without a trailing space character).
actions: Process reply code without accompanying text

statements.subject: server
statements.description: An SMTP server SHOULD send only the reply codes listed in this document.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: An SMTP server SHOULD use the text shown in the examples whenever appropriate.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: An SMTP client MUST determine its actions only by the reply code, not by the text (except for the "change of address" 251 and 551 and, if necessary, 220, 221, and 421 replies); in the general case, any text, including no text at all (although senders SHOULD NOT send bare codes), MUST be acceptable.
actions: Determine next action based on reply code only, not reply text

statements.subject: server
statements.description: An SMTP client MUST determine its actions only by the reply code, not by the text (except for the "change of address" 251 and 551 and, if necessary, 220, 221, and 421 replies); in the general case, any text, including no text at all (although senders SHOULD NOT send bare codes), MUST be acceptable.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: An SMTP client MUST determine its actions only by the reply code, not by the text (except for the "change of address" 251 and 551 and, if necessary, 220, 221, and 421 replies); in the general case, any text, including no text at all (although senders SHOULD NOT send bare codes), MUST be acceptable.
actions: Accept reply regardless of text content or absence of text

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: Whenever possible, a receiver-SMTP SHOULD test the first digit (severity indication) of the reply code.
actions: Test first digit of reply code to determine severity category

statements.subject: smtp
statements.description: The list of codes that appears below MUST NOT be construed as permanent.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: Consequently, a sender-SMTP MUST be prepared to handle codes not specified in this document and MUST do so by interpreting the first digit only.
actions: Handle reply code not listed in specification

statements.subject: client
statements.description: Consequently, a sender-SMTP MUST be prepared to handle codes not specified in this document and MUST do so by interpreting the first digit only.
actions: Interpret only first digit of unspecified reply code to determine next action

statements.subject: server
statements.description: In the absence of extensions negotiated with the client, SMTP servers MUST NOT send reply codes whose first digits are other than 2, 3, 4, or 5.
actions: Restrict reply codes to those whose first digit is in {2, 3, 4, 5}

statements.subject: client
statements.description: Clients that receive such out-of-range codes SHOULD normally treat them as fatal errors and terminate the mail transaction.
actions: Treat out-of-range reply code as fatal error
